For learning and teaching

Ready-made Swedish lessons

Full lessons on topics people really talk about in Sweden: a text, new vocabulary, exercises and speaking tasks. For self-study – and for teachers who need ready-made lesson material.

What’s included in a lesson

Every lesson comes as four PDF files, plus online versions in Canva and Miro for use in lessons:

🖥️

Student slides

The lesson as a presentation – from warm-up to mini-project.

✅

Slides with answers

The same presentation with answers – for the teacher or for self-checking.

📄

A4 worksheet

All the lesson’s exercises on sheets that are easy to print.

📝

A4 worksheet with answers

Answer keys to every exercise.

🎨

Canva presentation

An online version of the slides with answers – handy to show during a lesson.

🧩

Miro board

Student slides on an online whiteboard – for online lessons.

Lessons

Choose a topic and level

Level
Topic

Sverige på riktigt

Sweden beyond the textbook

B1–B2Sweden beyond the textbook

Vad är egentligen lagom?

What lagom really means – a word that explains a lot about the Swedish character. You read its story, work out where “in moderation” is appropriate, and together come up with tips for a newcomer: how to be lagom at work, in the neighbourhood or at a celebration.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
A2–B1Sweden beyond the textbook

Får man prata med främlingar på bussen?

Is it normal to talk to strangers on the bus – and which unwritten rules apply in Swedish public spaces? You learn to talk about rules with får, måste, behöver inte and brukar, and write a short scene about a small misunderstanding.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
A2–B1Sweden beyond the textbook

Fredagsmys – Sveriges heligaste kväll?

Fredagsmys – a cosy Friday evening that Swedes treat almost as a ritual. You read about this tradition, learn adverbs of frequency (alltid, ofta, ibland, sällan, aldrig) and plan the perfect Friday together.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B1Sweden beyond the textbook

Fika – mer än bara kaffe

Fika is not just coffee and a bun but a Swedish break for conversation and community. This lesson is shorter than the others: a text about fika, comprehension exercises, new words and a task where you put five fika-related things in order of importance and compare with a partner.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
A2Sweden beyond the textbook

Varför tar svenskar av sig skorna?

Why Swedes take off their shoes when they go to someone’s home – and how to remind people of it politely. You practise reflexive pronouns (ta av sig skorna) and, in a group, design the perfect hallway of a Swedish home with a sign saying “Ta av er skorna!”

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B1–B2Sweden beyond the textbook

Sambo, särbo eller gift?

Sambo, särbo or gift – three ways of living together in Sweden. You read about each of them, learn to compare (vanligare, vanligast, bättre, bäst) and choose which option suits a fictional couple best.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
A2–B1Sweden beyond the textbook

Varför står svenskar i kö så snällt?

Why Swedes queue so patiently – and how to describe who is standing where. You learn prepositions of place (framför, bakom, bredvid, mellan) and write a short scene in which someone jumps the queue.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B2–C1Sweden beyond the textbook

Jantelagen – finns den fortfarande?

Jantelagen – the unwritten rules of modesty known from Sandemose’s novel. Do they still apply in modern Sweden? You read, learn abstract nouns ending in -het (jämlikhet, blygsamhet, trygghet) and, in groups, hold a debate for and against.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B1–B2Sweden beyond the textbook

Systembolaget – varför kan man inte köpa vin i mataffären?

Why you can’t buy wine in a supermarket in Sweden – and why there is a state-run alcohol shop. You learn to talk about age (fylla 20 år, vara över 18) and make a poster or leaflet about Swedish alcohol rules for a friend who has just moved.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B1–B2Sweden beyond the textbook

Allemansrätten – får man verkligen gå nästan överallt?

Allemansrätten – the right to walk, pick berries and sleep in a tent almost anywhere in nature, but subject to certain rules. You learn prepositions of movement (genom, längs, in i, över, förbi) and draw a map of a walk, explaining what is allowed at each stop.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson

Svenska som svenskar faktiskt talar

Real spoken Swedish

B1–B2Real spoken Swedish

Ju, väl, nog och egentligen – små ord, stor skillnad

Four small words that change the tone of a whole sentence. You find out what ju, väl, nog and egentligen mean and learn to soften direct phrases so that you sound natural in Swedish – in a “before and after” exercise.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B1–B2Real spoken Swedish

”Vi får se” betyder kanske nej

Why the Swedish “Vi får se” often means “probably not” – and how to avoid going wrong when decoding evasive answers. You learn the construction det beror på + vad / om / hur / vem and find out what people really mean.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
A2–B1Real spoken Swedish

”Det blir bra” – svenskarnas universalsvar

“Det blir bra” – a favourite Swedish phrase for reassurance. You learn the difference between bli and vara (blir bra, blir kallt, blir svårt) and write a warm note to a friend who is worried.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B1–B2Real spoken Swedish

Asså, typ, liksom…

Asså, typ, liksom – the filler words that real spoken Swedish can’t do without. You work out when they sound natural, match them with their formal equivalents and write a dialogue that sounds authentic.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B1–B2Real spoken Swedish

Orka! Palla! Lägg av!

Orka! Palla! Lägg av! – exclamations and words that Swedes use every day and textbooks skip. You learn the imperative (Lägg av! Sluta! Kom igen!) and put together a quick guide to reactions for a new student.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B2Real spoken Swedish

Vad menar svenskar när de säger ”intressant”?

What Swedes really mean when they say “intressant” or “inte dåligt”. You learn litotes – an understated expression that means more than it seems to – and write a polite but honest review of a mediocre film or restaurant.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B1–B2Real spoken Swedish

Hur säger man nej utan att säga nej?

How to say no politely and still be understood. You learn polite refusal formulas (tyvärr, jag skulle gärna men…) and the construction hellre … än, and write a short, tactful message – declining an invitation or a request for help.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
A2–B1Real spoken Swedish

Tack tack, hej hej, ja ja – varför säger svenskar allt två gånger?

Why Swedes say tack tack, hej hej, ja ja – and what each of these doublings means. You look at doubled words, get a feel for when they fit and put together a mini-dictionary with examples.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B1Real spoken Swedish

Det ordnar sig! – 15 vardagsfraser

Fifteen everyday phrases Swedes use to encourage and reassure people – from “det ordnar sig” to “ta det piano”. You learn reflexive verbs for things working themselves out (ordna sig, klara sig, reda sig, lösa sig) and create a game for matching phrases to situations.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B2–C1Real spoken Swedish

Svenska som aldrig står i läroboken

Swedish that isn’t in the textbooks: abbreviations, reactions and colloquial words like oxå, iaf, najs. You learn how such abbreviations are formed and write a “coded” text message for another pair to decipher.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson

Psykologi & människan

Psychology and people

B1–B2Psychology and people

Varför skjuter vi upp saker?

Why we put things off even when we know it will get worse. You read what researchers think about it, learn the future tense (ska, tänker, kommer att) and break a “scary” task into five small steps together.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
A2–B1Psychology and people

Är du introvert eller extrovert?

Introvert or extrovert – or a bit of both? You learn the constructions både … och, antingen … eller and varken … eller, run a small survey in class and report the results.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B1–B2Psychology and people

Varför jämför vi oss med andra?

Why we compare ourselves with others – especially on social media. You learn adjectives and verbs with fixed prepositions (stolt över, nöjd med, avundsjuk på) and look at what stays “behind the scenes” of the perfect post.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B2–C1Psychology and people

Impostor syndrome – varför känner vi oss som bluffar?

Impostor syndrome: why some people feel like frauds even when they’ve succeeded. You learn to talk about feelings and impressions (känna sig, kännas, verka, se ut) and write the script for a one-minute podcast episode on the topic.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B1–B2Psychology and people

Kan man lära sig att bli lyckligare?

Can you learn to be happier? You read what research says about it, learn the difference between perfekt and preteritum when reporting scientific findings, and write a “news story” about a made-up study – purely for practice.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B1–B2Psychology and people

Varför är det så svårt att ändra en vana?

Why it’s so hard to change a habit – and what is actually known about it. You learn the construction det är svårt / lätt / viktigt att … and, in a group, play “myth or fact” about habits.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B2Psychology and people

Övertänkande – när hjärnan aldrig stänger av

When your mind won’t switch off: the difference between “fundera” and “älta”. You learn the construction sitta / ligga / stå / gå + och + verb (sitta och älta) and draw a “decision tree” for a thought going round in circles.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B1–B2Psychology and people

Vad gör oss motiverade?

What motivates us: from within or from outside, “lust eller lön”. You learn the constructions göra + adjective and få någon att + infinitive, and then present your own idea that helps people stay motivated – an app, a club or a challenge.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B2–C1Psychology and people

Kan man verkligen förändra sin personlighet?

Can you change your personality – and how far? You learn to use sin / sitt / sina and hans / hennes / deras correctly (the Ukrainian “свій”, meaning “one’s own”, helps here) and create a life timeline for an imaginary person who changed their behaviour.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
B2Psychology and people

Varför bryr vi oss så mycket om vad andra tycker?

Why do we worry so much about what others think – and do they notice us as much as we imagine (spotlighteffekten)? You learn causal conjunctions (eftersom, därför att, på grund av, tack vare) and plan a small, safe experiment.

4 PDF · Canva · MiroAsk about this lesson
